item.title: South Africa: High Court examines asylum seekers' detention at Lindela centre
item.description: South Africa's High Court judges visited the Lindela Repatriation Centre in Krugersdorp this week, ahead of delivering a ruling on 33 urgent applications concerning the detention of asylum seekers. The court is examining conflicting interpretations of a Constitutional Court ruling that prohibits the deportation of asylum seekers whose claims are still being processed. The case comes amid a wider and increasingly tense debate over immigration in South Africa, which has at times spilled over into deadly xenophobic violence. FRANCE 24's Eunice Masson reports from Cape Town, South Africa. Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.title: ‘You’ve got me for life’: first ceremonies in England cement care leavers’ relationships
item.description: Lifelong guardianship ceremonies were announced in July as way to publicly affirm chosen connections Allan was 14 years old and had been through eight foster families and a stint in a children’s home when he began living with foster carer Russ in Kettering – a move that would change the course of his life. Russ, 63, fought for Allan to get the school placements he needed and took him to kickboxing every week, eventually joining in himself. When Allan turned 18, he moved out into his own flat, but the pair have stayed close. Continue reading... Fuente: The Guardian - World.

item.title: Home Office tells woman born and raised in London she is not British
item.description: Woman, 24, says she cannot work and faces destitution after it was discovered her mother had no right to UK passport A 24-year-old woman who was born and raised in London believing she was a British citizen has been left in a state of shock after being told by authorities that she is not British . After the Home Office recently discovered that the woman’s mother, who is from Jamaica, had no right to a British passport, she received a letter informing her her UK passport would be revoked on March 11, 2026. It was due to expire in 2031. Continue reading... Fuente: The Guardian - World.

item.title: 'Our culture and identity': Deaf Nigerians embrace indigenous sign languages
item.description: With a quick flick of the wrist, Umaru Zayyanu conveys the phrase "I am a Nigerian". But the 37-year-old is not signing, rather in the west African nation's official sign language. Instead, he's using Hausa sign language. Such indigenous sign languages abound in Africa's most populous country, where deaf people were communicating with each other long before the advent of formal sign language taught in deaf schools, in 1960. Publicado también por: Africanews. Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.title: France awaits verdict in landmark police brutality trial over Michel Zecler assault
item.description: A French prosecutor on Thursday urged a court to jail three policemen who beat up a black music producer to four to six years, in a rare case of alleged police brutality to go to criminal court. The assault on Michel Zecler, now 47, triggered renewed outrage in France over police violence, which victims and researchers say is systemic but authorities and law enforcement unions claim is limited to isolated cases. item.title: Outcry as fossil fuels scrubbed from draft UN climate deal
